planned_meeting.purpose: Discuss older-adult representation in LUMINOSITY and the questions investigated by AbbVie in TeliMET NSCLC-01

interactions.purpose: Discuss older-adult representation in the published LUMINOSITY study
interactions.observation: The KOL asked how older adults were represented in LUMINOSITY and what population limitations should be discussed.
interactions.msl_response: I reviewed the published cohort with you: the updated analysis included 172 treated participants, with a median age of 64.5 years (range 33–83). The publication does not provide an age-stratified efficacy conclusion in its abstract, so I would avoid inferring how older adults fare from the overall response estimate. We agreed to keep age range, eligibility and subgroup-data availability visible in the source note.
interactions.msl_interpretation: The KOL may want a clearer summary of population characteristics and limitations. Draft interpretation, not a quote or validated insight.
interactions.task: Locate a suitable reviewed source pack and prepare a response draft.

interactions.observation: The KOL asked what AbbVie is investigating in TeliMET NSCLC-01 and how its question differs from the LUMINOSITY publication.
interactions.msl_response: I explained that TeliMET NSCLC-01 is a phase 3 registry study comparing telisotuzumab vedotin with docetaxel in previously treated, c-Met protein-overexpressing, non-squamous NSCLC. That is a comparative trial question; LUMINOSITY was a phase 2 single-arm study. The registry describes the planned study, so we should not present it as published comparative results.
interactions.msl_interpretation: The question remains relevant to the next meeting because the prior task is still open. Draft interpretation.
interactions.task: Review the TeliMET registry design alongside the LUMINOSITY publication and confirm which outcome results are available.

interactions.purpose: Clarify the requested source format before the next scientific meeting
interactions.observation: The KOL requested a concise source list linking publications and trial records, with explicit limitations and unresolved questions.
interactions.msl_response: I agreed to organize the follow-up into publication findings, registry design/status and questions the records do not answer. I also confirmed that registry endpoints are planned measures, while only posted results or a publication support outcome statements. The comparison remains open until the source list is reviewed together.
interactions.msl_interpretation: A structured, source-linked preparation format may help the next exchange. Draft interpretation only.
interactions.task: Prepare a source list separating published findings, registry design and unresolved questions.

interactions.observation: The KOL asked what information an evidence summary should include to support testing-related discussion.
interactions.msl_response: I suggested a source note that names the disease setting, biomarker, specimen and testing method, then separates evidence from implementation considerations. The cited consensus paper discusses both tissue and liquid biopsy approaches and their challenges in NSCLC. It is a Singapore-focused consensus, so we should identify its setting and not treat it as a universal local testing pathway.

planned_meeting.purpose: Review the draft outline and clarify what should be sourced versus interpreted

interactions.purpose: Discuss study endpoints and evidence limitations in a fictional scenario
interactions.observation: The KOL asked how an evidence summary would distinguish a measured study outcome from an interpretation of broader relevance.
interactions.msl_response: I used the EPCORE NHL-1 two-year follow-up as an example: the publication reports an overall response rate of 63.1% and complete response rate of 40.1% in 157 participants, with a 25.1-month median follow-up. I pointed out that this was a single-arm study and the analysis cutoff was April 21, 2023; those reported results should remain distinct from any broader interpretation.
interactions.msl_interpretation: The KOL may value explicit separation of reported outcomes from contextual interpretation. Draft interpretation, not a quote or validated insight.
interactions.task: Prepare a source-linked outline distinguishing reported outcomes, limitations, and interpretation.

interactions.purpose: Follow up on the proposed outline and confirm the next discussion question
interactions.observation: The KOL asked that the outline clearly identify where source evidence ends and interpretation begins.
interactions.msl_response: I brought back a revised outline with each outcome beside its citation and data cutoff, followed by a separate section for interpretation and unanswered questions. We agreed that the single-arm design and follow-up duration stay attached to the results so they are not lost when the findings are summarized.
interactions.msl_interpretation: Preserve source references next to each scientific statement and label synthesis as interpretation. Draft interpretation.
interactions.task: Review the revised outline and confirm the design, data cutoff and limitations remain visible.
